literal: It also meant strong ministers.
idiomatic: The same anomaly further signaled overbearing ministers.

literal: In the sixth month, the Great White was seen in daytime, in the Seven Stars.
idiomatic: That June Venus shone by day among the Seven Stars (Sagittarius).

literal: On day Yiyou, the Great White transgressed the Ghost Cart.
idiomatic: On yiyou Venus crossed the Ghost asterism.

literal: The prognostication states: "The state will have grief."
idiomatic: The gloss warns of national mourning.

literal: In the seventh month the emperor died; Huan Wen seized power by force of arms and was about to execute Wang Tanzhi and others; inside and outside there was coercion.
idiomatic: In July the sovereign passed away while Huan Wen bullied the court with troops, poised to kill Wang Tanzhi and allies, tightening pressure inside the palace and out.

literal: Moreover, Yu Xi entered the capital city; Lu Song entered the palace; both were exterminated.
idiomatic: Yu Xi marched on the capital and Lu Song burst into the palace; both risings were crushed.

literal: In Emperor Xiaowu’s first Ningkang year, first month, day Wushen, the moon covered the great star of the Heart.
idiomatic: Ningkang one, first month, wushen: the Moon occulted Antares.

literal: Investigating, the superior gloss states: "If the calamity is not on the king, then it is on Yu Province."
idiomatic: Commentary notes: if the throne escapes harm, Yu region still bears the blow.

literal: One gloss says: "The ruler’s mandate finds it ominous."
idiomatic: Another line warns the sovereign’s life-omen turns ill.

literal: In the third month, day Bingwu, the moon covered the fifth star of the Southern Dipper.
idiomatic: On bingwu in the third month the Moon occulted the Dipper’s fifth star.

literal: The prognostication states: "Great ministers will grieve; there will be deaths."
idiomatic: Senior officials face mourning and fatalities.

literal: One gloss says: "A general will die."
idiomatic: A variant singles out a field commander’s death.

literal: In the seventh month, Huan Wen died.
idiomatic: Huan Wen died in the seventh month.

literal: In the ninth month, day Guisi, Mars entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
idiomatic: On guisi in the ninth month Mars entered the Supreme Palace.

literal: At this time the empress dowager faced the court; government affairs had many shortcomings.
idiomatic: The regent empress held court while administration faltered.

literal: In the second year, intercalary month, day Jiwei, the moon covered the southern star of the Oxherd.
idiomatic: Leap month of year two, jiwei: the Moon occulted the Oxherd’s southern star.

literal: The prognostication states: "The left general will die."
idiomatic: Foretells the death of the left-side commander.

literal: In the twelfth month, day Jiashen, the Great White was seen in daytime, in the Root.
idiomatic: Twelfth month, jiashen: Venus shone by day in the Root (Dǐ).

literal: The Root is the field allotment of Yan Province.
idiomatic: Dǐ marks Yanzhou’s celestial territory.

literal: In the third year, fifth month, day Bingwu, North-of-the-River General Wang Tanzhi died.
idiomatic: Third year, fifth month, bingwu: North-of-the-River general Wang Tanzhi passed away.

literal: In the third year, sixth month, day Xinmao, the Great White transgressed the Eastern Well.
idiomatic: Sixth month, xinmao: Venus crossed the Eastern Well.

literal: The prognostication states: "The Qin region will have arms."
idiomatic: Foretells warfare in the old Qin heartland.

literal: In the ninth month, day Wushen, Mars covered the Left Law Enforcer.
idiomatic: Ninth month, wushen: Mars occulted the Left Law Enforcer star.

literal: The prognostication states: "Law enforcers will die."
idiomatic: Judicial officials face execution or death.

literal: In the first Taiyuan year, Fu Jian broke Liangzhou.
idiomatic: Taiyuan one: Fu Jian conquered Liangzhou.

literal: In the tenth month of the second year, Director of the Secretariat Wang Biaozhi died.
idiomatic: Second year’s tenth month: chief minister Wang Biaozhi died.

literal: In Taiyuan first year, fourth month, day Bingxu, Mars transgressed the third star of the Southern Dipper.
idiomatic: Taiyuan one, fourth month, bingxu: Mars crossed the Dipper’s third star.

literal: On day Bingshen, it again covered the fourth star.
idiomatic: On bingshen Mars also occulted the fourth star.

literal: The prognostication states: "Arms will rise greatly; the central lands will hunger."
idiomatic: Mass mobilization and famine stalk the heartland.

literal: One gloss says: "There will be an amnesty."
idiomatic: Another line allows for a general pardon.

literal: In the eighth month, day Guiyou, the Great White was seen in daytime, in the Root.
idiomatic: Eighth month, guiyou: Venus appeared by day in the Root.

literal: The Root is the field allotment of Yan Province.
idiomatic: Again Dǐ ties the sign to Yanzhou.

literal: In the ninth month, Mars transgressed the Weeping star, then entered the Feathered Forest.
idiomatic: September: Mars crossed the Weeping star and marched into the Feathered Forest guard asterism.

literal: The prognostication states: "The Son of Heaven will have weeping affairs; the central army’s troops will rise."
idiomatic: Royal mourning and palace-guard mobilization follow.

literal: In the eleventh month, day Jiwei, the moon covered the horn of the Root.
idiomatic: Eleventh month, jiwei: the Moon occulted the Root’s horn.

literal: The prognostication states: "Under Heaven there will be arms."
idiomatic: War spreads across the realm.

literal: One gloss says: "The state will have grief."
idiomatic: Another gloss stresses national mourning.

literal: In the second year, second month, Mars guarded the Feathered Forest.
idiomatic: Second year, second month: Mars stationed in the Feathered Forest.

literal: The prognostication states: "Palace-guard troops will rise greatly."
idiomatic: Elite household regiments swell in mutiny or campaign.

literal: In the ninth month, day Renwu, the Great White was seen in daytime, in the Horn.
idiomatic: Ninth month, renwu: Venus shone by day in the Horn.

literal: The Horn is the field allotment of Yan Province.
idiomatic: The Horn marks Yanzhou’s field.

literal: In the fifth month of the first Shengping year, a great amnesty was proclaimed.
idiomatic: Shengping one, fifth month: a sweeping pardon.

literal: In the eighth month of the third year, Qin raiders struck Fan, Deng, Xiangyang, and Pengcheng.
idiomatic: Third year, eighth month: Former Qin forces hit Fan, Deng, Xiangyang, and Pengcheng.

literal: In the fourth year’s second month, Xiangyang fell and Zhu Xu was captured.
idiomatic: Fourth year, second month: Xiangyang fell; Zhu Xu was taken.

literal: In the fourth month, Weixing fell; bandits gathered at Guangling and Sanhe, fifty or sixty thousand strong.
idiomatic: April: Weixing collapsed; rebels massed fifty to sixty thousand between Guangling and the Sanhe region.

literal: Thereupon the various armies encamped outward at choke points, and the governor of Danyang garrisoned the capital approaches.
idiomatic: Imperial columns sealed the passes while the Danyang governor fortified the approaches to the capital.

literal: In the sixth month, Inspector of Yan Province Xie Xuan attacked the bandits and crushed them.
idiomatic: June: Yan inspector Xie Xuan smashed the rebel host.

literal: At this time inner and outer realms were linked in warfare, year after year of dearth.
idiomatic: Civil war raged on all sides amid successive famines.

literal: In the fourth year, eleventh month, day Dingsi, the Great White transgressed the Weeping star.
idiomatic: Fourth year, eleventh month, dingsi: Venus crossed the Weeping star.

literal: The prognostication states: "The Son of Heaven will have weeping affairs."
idiomatic: Royal tears and state funerals were portended.

literal: In the fifth year, seventh month, day Bingzi, Mercury transgressed the Coachman.
idiomatic: Fifth year, seventh month, bingzi: Mercury crossed Xuanyuan.

literal: The prognostication states: "The queen consort will answer for it."
idiomatic: The empress bears the omen.

literal: In the ninth month, day Guiwei, Empress Wang died.
idiomatic: September, guiwei: Empress Wang passed away.

literal: Sixth year, ninth month, day Bingzi.
idiomatic: Sixth year, ninth month, bingzi (date anchor).

literal: The Great White was seen in daytime.
idiomatic: Venus shone in daylight.

literal: In the eleventh month of the seventh year, the Great White again was seen in daytime, in the Dipper.
idiomatic: Seventh year, eleventh month: Venus reappeared by day in the Dipper.

literal: The prognostication states: "Wu will have arms and mourning."
idiomatic: The southeast (Wu lands) faces war and funerals.

literal: In the eighth year, fourth month, day Jiazi, the Great White again was seen in daytime, in Orion’s Belt.
idiomatic: Eighth year, fourth month, jiazi: Venus again shone by day in Orion.

literal: The prognostication states: "Wei will have arms and mourning."
idiomatic: The heartland Wei zone faces battle and bereavement.

literal: That month, Huan Chong campaigned in the Han River basin and Yang Liang attacked Shu, both seizing cities and taking territory.
idiomatic: That same month Huan Chong drove up the Han while Yang Liang struck Shu; both columns took towns and ground.

literal: In the eighth month, Fu Jian personally commanded, claiming a million; in the ninth month he captured and destroyed Shouyang.
idiomatic: August: Fu Jian took the field at the head of a host styled a million; September saw Shouyang fall.

literal: In the tenth month, Liu Laozhi defeated Fu Jian’s general Liang Cheng, beheaded him, and killed or captured more than ten thousand.
idiomatic: October: Liu Laozhi routed Liang Cheng, Fu Jian’s general, took his head, and piled up over ten thousand casualties and captives.

literal: Xie Xuan and others again defeated Fu Jian at the Fei River, beheaded his younger brother Rong, and Fu Jian’s great host fled in collapse.
idiomatic: Xie Xuan’s coalition broke Fu Jian on the Fei, slew his brother Fu Rong, and scattered the mass army.

literal: In the ninth year’s sixth month, Empress Dowager Chu died.
idiomatic: Ninth year, June: Empress Dowager Chu died.

literal: In the eighth month, Xie Xuan marched out and encamped at Pengcheng, planning the central plain.
idiomatic: August: Xie Xuan advanced to garrison Pengcheng, eyeing the Central Plain.

literal: In the ninth year, seventh month, day Bingxu, the Great White was seen in daytime.
idiomatic: Ninth year, seventh month, bingxu: Venus by day.

literal: On day Dingsi in the eleventh month, it again was seen in daytime.
idiomatic: Eleventh month, dingsi: another daylight Venus.

literal: On day Yihai in the tenth year’s fourth month, it again was seen in daytime in the Net and Hairy Head.
idiomatic: Tenth year, fourth month, yihai: Venus again blazed by day through Bi and the Pleiades.

literal: The prognostication states: "The Wei state will have arms and mourning."
idiomatic: The Wei heartland faces war and death.

literal: At this time Fu Jian’s great host had scattered; Zhao and Wei linked arms in mutual attack; Fu Jian was killed by Yao Chang.
idiomatic: Fu Jian’s army had melted away; northern rivals tore at each other until Yao Chang slew Fu Jian.

literal: In the eleventh year, third month, day Wushen, the Great White was seen in daytime, in the Eastern Well.
idiomatic: Eleventh year, third month, wushen: Venus by day in the Eastern Well.

literal: The prognostication states: "Qin will have arms; ministers will be strong."
idiomatic: Qin lands see war and domineering ministers.

literal: In the sixth month, day Jiashen, it again was seen in daytime in the Ghost Cart.
idiomatic: Sixth month, jiashen: daylight Venus in the Ghost asterism.

literal: The prognostication states: "Qin will have arms."
idiomatic: Again: warfare in Qin.

literal: At the time Wei, Yao Chang, and Fu Deng linked arms, campaigning without cease.
idiomatic: Wei, Yao Chang, and Fu Deng kept armies in the field without pause.

literal: On day Jiawu, Jupiter was seen in daytime, in the Stomach.
idiomatic: Jiawu: Jupiter shone by day in the Stomach lodge.

literal: The prognostication states: "Lu will have arms; ministers will be strong."
idiomatic: Lu’s territory faces war; ministers grow overbearing.

literal: In the twelfth year, Murong Chui raided Dong’e, Zhai Liao raided the Yellow River line, Yao Chang assumed a reign title at Anding, Fu Deng set himself up on Long, and Lü Guang seized Liang.
idiomatic: Twelfth year: Murong Chui struck Dong’e, Zhai Liao harried the He frontier, Yao Chang styled himself at Anding, Fu Deng held Long, and Lü Guang carved out Liangzhou.

literal: In the twelfth year, sixth month, day Guimao, the Great White was seen in daytime, in the Willow.
idiomatic: Twelfth year, sixth month, guimao: Venus by day in the Willow.

literal: On day Gengwu in the tenth month, the Great White was seen in daytime, in the Dipper.
idiomatic: Tenth month, gengwu: daylight Venus in the Dipper.

literal: On day Bingxu in the thirteenth year’s first month, it again was seen in daytime.
idiomatic: Thirteenth year, first month, bingxu: another daylight Venus.

literal: In the twelfth month, Mars stood in the Horn and Neck, its color and form fierce and strong.
idiomatic: December: Mars blazed angrily through Horn and Neck.

literal: The prognostication states: "When Mars loses its norm, clerks will abandon their laws and feudal lords will disorder their government."
idiomatic: Erratic Mars means collapsing bureaucracy and rebel barons.

literal: From this time Murong Chui, Zhai Liao, Yao Chang, Fu Deng, and Murong Yong all blocked roads with arms and vied for supremacy.
idiomatic: Afterward Murong Chui, Zhai Liao, Yao Chang, Fu Deng, and Murong Yong all kept private armies and fought for dominance.

literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year, Pengcheng’s occult bandits again proclaimed a title at Huangqiu; Liu Laozhi destroyed them.
idiomatic: Fourteenth year, first month: Pengcheng rebels styled themselves at Huangqiu until Liu Laozhi wiped them out.

literal: In the third month, Zhang Dao broke Hexiang, besieged Taishan, and Xiang Qinzhi drove him off.
idiomatic: March: Zhang Dao took Hexiang and ringed Taishan until Xiang Qinzhi repulsed him.

literal: That year Zhai Liao again took Xingyang and raided Chen and Xiang.
idiomatic: That year Zhai Liao seized Xingyang and scourged Chen and Xiang.

literal: At that time government had many abuses and the ruler’s way declined.
idiomatic: Administration rotted while royal authority slid.

literal: In the fourteenth year, fourth month, day Yisi, the Great White was seen in daytime in the Willow.
idiomatic: Fourteenth year, fourth month, yisi: Venus by day in the Willow.

literal: On day Xinmao in the sixth month, it again was seen in daytime in the Wings.
idiomatic: Sixth month, xinmao: daylight Venus in the Wings.

literal: On day Bingyin in the ninth month, it again was seen in daytime in the Chariot.
idiomatic: September, bingyin: daylight Venus in the Chariot.

literal: In the twelfth month, Mars entered the Feathered Forest.
idiomatic: December: Mars entered the Feathered Forest.

literal: The prognostications were all the same as above.
idiomatic: The glosses matched those cited earlier.

literal: In the fifteenth year, Zhai Liao plundered Si and Yan; the massed armies repeatedly campaigned without success; Murong Chui also overran Bing, Ji, and neighboring provinces.
idiomatic: Fifteenth year: Zhai Liao raided Si and Yan while imperial columns failed to finish him; Murong Chui meanwhile overran Bing and Ji.

literal: In the seventh month there was drought.
idiomatic: July brought drought.

literal: In the eighth month the commanderies suffered great floods, and Yanzhou also had locusts.
idiomatic: August floods swamped the districts and locusts scourged Yanzhou.

literal: In the fifteenth year, ninth month, day Guiwei, Mars entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
idiomatic: Fifteenth year, September, guiwei: Mars entered the Supreme Palace.

literal: In the tenth month, the Great White entered the Feathered Forest.
idiomatic: October: Venus marched into the Feathered Forest.

literal: On the new moon of day Guimao in the sixteenth year’s fourth month, the Great White was seen in daytime.
idiomatic: Sixteenth year, fourth month, guimao new moon: Venus visible by day.

literal: In the eleventh month, day Guisi, the moon covered the front star of the Heart.
idiomatic: Eleventh month, guisi: the Moon occulted the Heart’s forward star.
